svg.aria-label: Scribobulate system overview: one single-threaded process; document windows of tabs over a split source/preview view; Markdown flowing through CriticMarkup extraction, pulldown-cmark and the renderer into the preview; document I/O through docio on GLib's thread pool; and a second, display-free consumer of the same event stream that exports the document to HTML and PDF.
svg.title: Scribobulate system overview
svg.text: Scribobulate — one process, one thread
GtkApplication · app-id com.extollit.scribobulate · every module runs on the GLib main loop (no worker threads, no channels)
Single instance (HANDLES_OPEN): a second launch with file arguments forwards its argv over D-Bus to this process — no second process starts.
--new-instance opts out; it is stripped from argv in main() before registration, because registration forwards argv before any handler runs.
Document Window (1..N)
WindowChrome — per window, shared by every tab
menu bar · toolbar · outline + annotations sidebar · conflict + info toasts · status bar · zoom level
TabView — custom TabBar + GtkStack (deliberately not GtkNotebook)
Tab = one Document (1..N) — TabState, keyed by a stable TabId
TabId survives a cross-window move, so a tab can be rehomed without rebuilding it
TabState (the document model)
path · source · saved_baseline · editor_buf · file_monitor · search_context
SplitView — one custom widget, three children mounted once
modes Preview | Edit | Split are pure layout parameters: a hidden pane is set_child_visible(false),
never reparented — the editor's lifetime is what makes that non-negotiable
Source pane
sourceview5::View
GtkSourceView 5 — editable,
own style scheme + undo stack.
Reused for the tab's whole life.
Preview pane
CodePreviewView
GtkTextView subclass — self-draws
code/quote backgrounds + gutter.
Rebuilt on each render.
Split adds orientation, pane order, and a fraction (a ratio, not pixels — so the divider survives a resize).
Anchored children inside the preview buffer: tables (custom ScribTableWidget), images, horizontal rules.
Comment entry floats on a GtkOverlay; the marker card is a GtkPopover subclass re-anchored on scroll.
Editor edits and preview annotations both write the tab's one canonical editor buffer.
Render pipeline
Markdown source → real GTK widgets. No HTML engine.
annotate:: extract
strips CriticMarkup → cleaned text + shifts table
pulldown-cmark (md_options)
explicit extension allowlist, never Options::all() —
an unhandled extension must degrade to literal text
renderer::Renderer
walks the event stream → GtkTextBuffer + named tags
syntect highlights fenced code as per-token tags
preview::build_render_products
buffer · source map · copy map · links · anchored
children · code/quote ranges · headings · markers
— the typed outputs the view installs in lockstep
preview::render / re_render / splice
Three paths: render appends; re_render swaps the buffer,
keeping widgets but NOT the reading position (it re-anchors);
splice rewrites one fold's region, keeping widgets and place.
Preview styling = the active reading theme (themes.toml,
data); System probes the live GTK theme. A theme or
desktop change re-renders every tab; split waits 300 ms.
The outline sidebar parses the same source separately,
keying headings by source byte offset — so it works in
all three modes, including Edit (which has no preview).
source text
widgets
Markdown file (.md)
the only document Scribobulate owns —
no database, no sidecar, no cache;
the file on disk is the source of truth
Save — window/save.rs
Guarded on content, not mtime: the on-disk bytes are
re-read and compared against saved_baseline, so a
coarse filesystem clock cannot mask a real conflict.
atomic_io::write_atomic — write-temp-then-rename,
so a crash mid-write can never truncate the file.
Live reload — gio::FileMonitor
connect_changed fires directly on the main loop — no
thread, no channel. One monitor per tab, per file.
winstate::external_change_action — a pure, GTK-free
decision core (unit-tested headlessly):
same content → Ignore · changed + dirty → Toast · changed + clean → Reload
read · docio
write · docio
reload / conflict toast
open / save
A save's own rename looks exactly like an external delete to GIO — the monitor is told to expect it.
Every arrow above runs on GLib's I/O thread pool via docio — never on the main thread, and capped so it cannot delay a recovery snapshot.
config.toml — XDG_CONFIG_HOME
Static user preferences, read once at startup.
No hot-reload. Distinct from session state.
Must be read before the redirect below moves the path.
session.toml — XDG_STATE_HOME
Windows, their tabs' paths, view modes, zoom.
No document text here — paths only (but see swap, below);
restored at startup when no window exists yet.
workaround.rs — GTK 4.6 only
Redirects XDG_CONFIG_HOME per-process to a synthesized
compose file, so a large ~/.XCompose can't crash GTK 4.6.
Symlinks the real config back in — that blast radius is wide.
scribobulate.log + crash-<stamp>-<pid>.log — XDG_STATE_HOME
Every info-or-worse record, appended unbuffered and size-capped — regardless of RUST_LOG; the last 64 are also held in a fixed-slot, lock-free ring in memory.
A panic or a fatal signal writes a report: build identity and fault first, then those breadcrumbs, then a backtrace and the process's executable mappings.
No document text is ever recorded — paths, sizes and event names only. The handler re-raises, so the process still dies from the signal that killed it.
Crash recovery — swap/ under XDG_STATE_HOME · swapfile/ + window/swap.rs + window/swaprecovery.rs
The one place document text is persisted, and only while a document is dirty. Invariant: a swap file exists iff the document is dirty,
applied at the single point dirtiness is recomputed — so save, undo, discard and reload need no deletion rule of their own.
Written by replace_contents_async (GLib's thread pool — no thread of ours; owner-only from the first byte). Each file carries a
frontmatter header naming its own document, so recovery reads the headers, never session.toml: a non-empty swap/ IS the "unclean exit" signal.
Network — imagefetch.rs · the process's ONLY outbound connection, and only with "Show Unsafe Images" on
An in-process HTTPS GET (system trust store, system proxy), not a URI handed to GIO: GIO resolves http/https only where a backend claims the scheme — a
daemon on Linux, an in-DLL VFS on Windows, nothing on macOS. Bounded by connect/global timeouts and a byte cap; blocks the main thread for the fetch.
GSK_RENDERER=cairo — set in main() before GTK initialises
The application never creates a GL/GLES context and never appears as a GPU client: 0 MiB VRAM, ~80 MiB RAM for a full-fidelity document.
This one line is why the whole stack is "GtkTextView + text tags + a few custom widgets" rather than an embedded web engine — measured, not assumed.
Export — the SECOND consumer of the same event stream (export/), never of the preview widget
Re-enters at annotate::extract and walks the same pulldown events, so a tab that was never rendered, an edit-only window and an unsaved buffer all export identically —
and the whole pipeline is display-free, so it sits inside the coverage gate. One ExportDoc, two sinks: html.rs serialises it; paginate.rs + pdf.rs measure with Pango and
draw through GtkPrintOperation to a staged temp, promoted only on success — GTK truncates a destination it is given before the first page is drawn.
